actions.justification: Mandatory first step per ACG GI bleeding guidelines. Patient has tachycardia (HR 128) and hypotension (BP 82/48), indicating hemorrhagic shock requiring immediate quantification.
Mandatory assessment to quantify degree of hemodynamic instability and guide resuscitation. MAP of 59 indicates significant shock requiring immediate intervention.
Mandatory — large-bore IV access required immediately for fluid resuscitation and medication administration in this hemodynamically unstable patient with massive GI bleed.
MANDATORY: CBC required to assess hemoglobin, hematocrit, and platelet count in the setting of massive GI hemorrhage. Per ACG guidelines, this is a required immediate action.
MANDATORY: Coagulation studies required in cirrhotic patient with active bleeding to assess INR/PT and guide transfusion strategy (FFP, platelets). Per ACG guidelines.
MANDATORY: Type and crossmatch essential for preparation of packed RBCs and blood products in this patient with massive hemorrhage and hemodynamic shock.

Patient is in hemorrhagic shock (MAP 59, HR 128, BP 82/48). ACG guidelines mandate immediate hemodynamic resuscitation with IV fluids before endoscopy. Crystalloid bolus is the first-line intervention for volume resuscitation.

Patient has known cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and prior variceal bleeding with active massive hematemesis. Octreotide (somatostatin analogue) reduces portal pressure and splanchnic blood flow, is indicated empirically for suspected variceal bleeding and should be started immediately alongside resuscitation.
Urgent GI consultation is required for emergent upper endoscopy (EGD) for diagnosis and treatment of suspected variceal hemorrhage. Endoscopy should follow hemodynamic stabilization per guidelines.
Serial CBC needed to trend hemoglobin given active hemorrhage and hemodynamic instability (HR 128, BP 82/48). Guides transfusion decisions per ACG guidelines (transfuse if Hgb <7).
Lactate helps assess severity of hemorrhagic shock and tissue hypoperfusion (MAP 59, HR 128). Guides resuscitation adequacy.
Although type and crossmatch was ordered initially, repeat/confirm crossmatch is needed to prepare packed RBCs for imminent transfusion given ongoing massive hematemesis and hemodynamic instability.

Hemoglobin is 6.2 g/dL, below the 7 g/dL threshold. Patient has hemodynamic instability (BP 82/48, HR 128). Packed RBC transfusion is required per ACG guidelines for resuscitation before endoscopy in this unstable patient with active variceal bleeding.

Prokinetic agent (erythromycin or metoclopramide) given pre-endoscopy improves gastric visualization by promoting gastric emptying of blood clots, increasing diagnostic yield of upper endoscopy in this patient with massive hematemesis.

BMP is needed to assess renal function (hepatorenal syndrome risk in cirrhosis), electrolytes, BUN (elevated BUN/Cr ratio supports upper GI bleeding), and glucose - all critical for managing this complex cirrhotic patient with massive GI hemorrhage.
Patient is hemodynamically unstable with Hgb 6.2 after PRBC transfusion initiated; repeat CBC needed to trend response to transfusion and guide further blood product therapy.
Initial lactate was ordered; repeat lactate is critical to assess adequacy of resuscitation and tissue perfusion in this patient with MAP 59 and hemorrhagic shock signs (HR 128, BP 82/48).
IV PPI is indicated as adjunct therapy in upper GI bleeding to reduce acid-related mucosal injury, even in variceal bleeding where mixed etiology is possible given cirrhosis history.
